newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-DuPont Q1 seen better,Dow to stall.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-DuPont Q1 seen better,Dow to stall.

text.p: EI DuPont & Nemours Co is set to continue strong earnings growth on the back of improved volumes in the first quarter of 1997, but Dow Chemical Co will be marred by low caustic soda prices.
First Call's consensus of analysts' forecasts for first quarter earnings per share before extraordinary items is $1.76 compared with $1.61 a year ago, growth of 9.3 percent.
DuPont is due to report on April 23.
"DuPont can keep in the high single digit volume growth, the company stands to do very, very well," said Theodore Semegran, chemicals analyst at Dean Witter.
He is forecasting $1.77 per share for the first quarter and $7.20 for the full year against $7.13 from First Call and $6.65 before extroardinary items in 1996.
"Our only concern is how long you can keep a company growing at two to three times gross domestic product growth," Semegran said.
Analysts say that Du Pont will not be a major beneficiary of any decline in energy prices, because of the contribution of its Conoco energy subsidiary.
There has been speculation DuPont might sell Conoco, but analysts are skeptical that the whole unit would be sold.
"Why sell the goose that lays the golden egg," says Bill Young of Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette.
"Although they should be doing something more active to turn around their downstream operations."
Last year, Conoco and Phillips Petroleum had talks on a refining and marketing merger but these collapsed.

Young is looking for EPS of $1.75 a share from DuPont in the first quarter. For Dow Chemical, which reports on April 24, Young is also looking for $1.75 a share compared with a consensus of $1.70 per share and $1.90 in the year ago period and $1.69 in the fourth quarter of 1996.
"The biggest factor for Dow is caustic soda prices, which are down a lot and Dow is the largest producer," the analyst said.
Dow accounts for around 28 percent of U.S. production and spot caustic soda prices are around $85 a ton on the west coast compared with $185 a year ago.
Dean Witter's Semegran is forecasting $1.70 per share and $7.50 for the full year against a First Call consensus of $7.16 for 1997 and an actual $7.16 for the whole of 1996.

For both Dow and Du Pont, analysts say that the strength of the dollar against European currencies and the Japanese yen will have little impact as raw material cost declines and other factors will mask the effect.

Looking further out, analysts warn there will be a substantial buildup in domestic bulk chemicals capacity, especially ethylene and its dervivatives, in the fourth quarter of this year and the start of 1997 which will have a large impact on earnings.
